source.title: Western lowland gorilla
source.quote: Males have an average weight of 140 kg (310 lb), females of 70 kg (150 lb).

mass_kg.note: Average adult male; range is the standard +/-10%.

source.title: Western gorilla
source.quote: Males average 1.67 m (5.5 ft) although reaching a height up to 1.76 m (5.8 ft)

size_m.note: Average standing height of adult males; range is the standard +/-10%.

top_speed_mps.note: No published top speed found for this animal; category default.

source.title: 9 jaw-dropping animals with the strongest bite (IFAW)
source.quote: The bite force of the Western gorilla (Gorilla gorilla) was calculated by one study to be about 3,420 Newtons.
source.license: Publisher copyright, not an open license; one sentence cited

attack_force_n.note: Modeled maximum molar bite from Eng, Lieberman, Zink and Peters 2013, Am. J. Phys. Anthropol. 151:544 (doi:10.1002/ajpa.22296), as quoted by IFAW; the paper itself was not readable here. A molar peak, so high for a fighting bite; range is +/-25%.

attacks_per_s.note: No published attack rate found for this animal; category default.

armor_0_1.note: armor level 1: fur and bare skin.

source.title: Observations of severe and lethal coalitionary attacks in wild mountain gorillas (Rosenbaum, Vecellio and Stoinski 2016, Scientific Reports 6:37018)
source.quote: Approximately 3-4 minutes after the attack began, it abruptly stopped.

endurance_s.note: Stand-in: a mountain gorilla group attack on a lone male, used for an adult male western lowland gorilla. Upper end of the stated range; the source gives no mean.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 3: defends itself and its troop, avoids risky fights.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 3: family troop that defends together.
